craft_notes: Sthāyin: one-yet-many by fitness. Sanskrit-first: yogyatā (FITNESS — fit seer meets fit seen, kept); bhāga (SHARES — held-in-common, not parts). Rows: 9 (one/many pair), 3 (fit-seer/fit-seen chiasmus — seer with seen across the line), 1 (‘shares’ closes — held-common last). Close: ‘breaks into shares’. Rupture: em-dash (one stated, then its breaking). Rejected: ‘parts’ — killed: shares held-in-common; ‘splits’ — killed: breaks (bheda breaks; splits severs). Read aloud: ONE, yet MAN-y — WHERE-fit-SEER meets FIT-seen … the SAME-light BREAKS in-to SHARES.

lines: One, yet many — where fit seer meets fit seen,
the same light breaks into shares.

reads_against.argmap: How does free consciousness become the bound knower? → Cause stated, means refused, manifold explained, veil named: descent promised.
c1_essence: Free consciousness causes, unborrowing opens, divides by fitness, veils by tightening — descent promised.
